data.title: Unit 1 : The Human Body
Brain, Heart and Lungs
data.heading: Lungs
data.text: The lungs help spread oxygen throughout the body, and get rid of carbon dioxide.
The two lungs are positioned around the heart.
The heart and the lungs are protected by the ribcage.
A human being breathes in about 10,000 litres of air every day, so the lungs are continuously at work.
As one breathes in, oxygen gets into the lungs. The oxygen is then transferred into the blood and pumped around the body.
When we breathe out, we get rid of carbon dioxide as it isn't needed by the body.
The diaphragm helps the lungs to take in air.
